europeRecord.statement: Let $0<x_1<\cdots<x_{2024}=1$. Colour 1012 entries red and the others blue, ordered as $r_i,b_i$, and put $S=\sum_{i=1}^{1012}r_i(b_i-b_{i-1})$, with $b_0=0$. (a) Can the $x_i$ be chosen so every colouring has $S<1/2$? (b) Prove some colouring has $S>x_{2023}/2$.

otherRecord.statement: Let $0<x_1<\cdots<x_{2024}=1$. Colour half the numbers red and half blue, listing each colour increasingly as $r_i,b_i$; put $b_0=0$ and $S=\sum_{i=1}^{1012}r_i(b_i-b_{i-1})$. (a) Show some choice of the $x_i$ makes every colouring satisfy $S<1/2$. (b) Show every choice admits a colouring with $S>x_{2023}/2$.

evidence: Identical ordered 2024 positive numbers, 1012 red/blue entries, the same telescoping sum, and the same two extremal assertions. The Armenian wording asks whether part (a) is possible; the Danish wording asks to prove it. Root reconciled the numerical ratings at 4.5 after deriving an original proof.

Base $\overline{BC}$ is the longest side of the isosceles triangle $ABC$. Let $M$ be a point on the side $\overline{BC}$ such that $|BM| = |AB|$. Point $N$ is the foot of the altitude from $M$ to $\overline{AB}$.
Prove that the triangle $BMN$ and the quadrilateral $ACMN$ have equal areas and equal perimeters. (United Kingdom 2018)

otherRecord.statement: In isosceles triangle $ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $BC$ is the longest side. Choose $N\in BC$ with $BN=AB$, and let $M$ be its perpendicular projection to $AB$. Prove line $MN$ bisects both the area and the perimeter of the triangle.

evidence: Same isosceles triangle, same point at distance AB along BC, and its perpendicular projection to AB. M and N are interchanged. Equal areas/perimeters of the resulting pieces is exactly simultaneous area/perimeter bisection. Croatia 2019 county Year 1 Variant A Q4 explicitly credits UK 2018. Europe rated 3.5 and therefore excluded; British rated 4.5 and included. Root should reconcile rating and retain the Croatian appearance.
action: Root review; no global bank changes made by Europe agent.
